evidence.summary: Approved design (2026-10-11) for a local, ad-hoc signed macOS arm64 build of LifeDashboard as a Tauri 2 app. Decisions: window on the API origin http://127.0.0.1:3101 (one origin keeps the session cookie and Host/Origin checks); fixed port 3101; Node 24 arm64 binary as Tauri sidecar; API bundled to one ESM file with Vite 8; separate data directory; pairing code read from API stdout and shown in a native dialog; startup code only without an unexpired session; static UI served by a small API handler; std::process::Command without tauri-plugin-shell; SIGTERM via /bin/kill; no tauri dev. Out of scope: Developer ID signing, notarization, universal or Intel builds, Windows and Linux, auto-update, tray, autostart, automatic API restart, native menu beyond default, moving dev data. Acceptance criteria 1-10 in the window (WebKit).

Ten tasks: API config and UI/runtime directories; sandbox runtime from runtimeDir; static UI with SPA fallback; startup pairing code only for unpaired installs; API bundle, ready line and smoke check; desktop package scaffold with Node sidecar (hardenedRuntime false); stdout line parsers with Rust tests; wrapper lifecycle and package build; documentation; manual acceptance. Appended section «Acceptance results (2026-10-11)»: items 1-10 recorded as pass, with evidence per item. Item 10 note: the expected pairing dialog before the error dialog did not appear because the install was already paired. Plan checkboxes and the automated check results (typecheck, test, cargo test, smoke:bundle) are not recorded in the plan.

risks.text: Several acceptance items used partner-confirmed gestures or dialogs (items 2, 4, 6 and 10 as recorded), and the pairing dialog could not be captured by window-scoped screenshots.
No code review of the desktop change is recorded.
The build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized; it is intended for the machine that built it (spec Decisions, Audience).

decisions.text: The window loads http://127.0.0.1:3101/ and the API serves the UI on the same origin. This keeps the SameSite=Strict session cookie, the Host and Origin allowlists and relative fetch URLs unchanged; a tauri:// origin would break auth in several places.
Fixed port 3101. A random port changes the origin and resets WebKit localStorage on every launch; 3101 does not collide with the dev API on 3001.
The API runs as a Node 24 arm64 binary shipped as a Tauri sidecar (externalBin). This works when the app starts from Finder, which has no nvm PATH.
The API is bundled into one ESM file with Vite 8. @lifedashboard/contracts exports .ts sources that Node does not strip under node_modules, so a copied node_modules would not start.
Separate data directory ~/Library/Application Support/LifeDashboard Desktop. db.ts assumes one process owns the database, and a newer dev schema would stop the app.
The wrapper reads the pairing code from the API's stdout and shows it in a native dialog. The security model is unchanged.
The API issues the startup pairing code only when no unexpired session exists. Otherwise the desktop app would show the dialog on every launch.
Static UI is served by a small handler in the API, with no @fastify/static, reusing the file-serving and path guards already in apps/api.
The sidecar is started with std::process::Command, not tauri-plugin-shell, and no capabilities are granted, so the remote page has no IPC access.
Shutdown sends SIGTERM through /bin/kill, then SIGKILL after 5 s. std::process::Child::kill sends SIGKILL directly, and this avoids a libc or nix dependency.

Hardened runtime is off (bundle.macOS.hardenedRuntime false). Re-signing the copied Node binary ad-hoc with hardened runtime and without JIT entitlements could break V8; hardened runtime matters only for notarization, which is out of scope.
No tauri dev. UI and API keep developing through pnpm dev; the desktop package has no build, dev, typecheck or test script, because the root pnpm build and pnpm dev would recurse into it.
